decisions: Append optional projectId and default-false unassigned to completion/Habit filters. Explicit project and unassigned cannot combine. Select exact current retained task.ProjectId, not accepted event snapshot placement.

Current Unassigned includes null placement and retained references to logically removed projects. Exact removed-project selection still matches the raw retained project ID. Archived but not removed projects remain assigned. Labels must distinguish all three cases and preserve exact IDs when names collide.

Keep original completion/Habit timestamp, accepted snapshot/current fallback text/notes, archive flags, restoration/correction references and precise stable ordering unchanged. Project/text/task/direction/kind/UTC predicates combine with AND before full counts/paging.

Expose optional currentPlacement metadata only for project/unassigned-filtered result rows. Include exact current project ID/name/archive/removal flags, unassigned state and currentRetainedTaskAssignment basis; never claim event-time project membership. Old unfiltered result encodings remain unchanged.
Missing exact project identities fail explicitly rather than silently broadening or implying an empty successful selection. Existing revision-bound paging continues unchanged.

The History route receives exact UUID project/unassigned selection plus optional Workspace/source guards from Projects links. Malformed or mismatched scope remains unavailable. Manual filter changes are explicit new reads; account/source changes clear private row/selection state.

Add per-project and general retained-history navigation to Projects. History selectors include retained archived/removed identities and disambiguate duplicate names by UUID. Existing exact-event restoration, linked/unknown refusal, original command recovery and separate extended recovery stay unchanged.

The existing archived/terminal recovery browser retains independent filters and clear scope wording. The new project selector applies to completion/Habit events, avoiding a duplicate recovery page or new recovery mutation contract.

Qualification requires independent cross-runtime current-versus-accepted-placement cases, full counts/stale pages, archived/removed/unassigned cases, original restore recovery, scoped navigation, actual local SDK/D1 and current Release light/obsidian phone/desktop normal/enlarged-text browser routes. No publication, real account, provider mutation or device operation is authorized by development qualification.

The browser history selector exposes retained archived/removed identities, while default list_projects exposes active records only. Extend the existing reviewed read-only list_projects tool and native parity helper with explicit includeRetained=true, preserving default active behavior and revision-bound paging. Agent workflows can choose duplicate/retired exact IDs without permanent browser automation.
